name: Ariane 1
best_known_for: Europe's first independent orbital launcher — three-stage hypergolic-then-cryogenic vehicle that opened the commercial-comsat era for ESA and launched Giotto to Halley's Comet
credit: Three-stage rocket (UH-25 / N2O4 first + second stage, LH₂ / LOX HM7 third stage) developed by the Centre national d'études spatiales (CNES) at the request of ESA after the cancelled Europa launcher line. 11 flights from Kourou between 1979-12-24 (L01, partial success) and 1986-02-22 (L11, last operational), with three failures. Carried 27 European telecom + science satellites including ECS-1, Marecs A/B, Spacenet, Telecom 1A/1B, and ESA's Giotto Halley flyby probe (1985-07-02). Retired after Ariane 2 / 3 / 4 expanded the family upward in payload capacity; the HM7 cryogenic upper-stage technology lived on through Ariane 4 and into Ariane 5's ESC-A second stage.
